summary: Harden the Namias portfolio against common web vulnerabilities. Add rate limiting to every API endpoint, scan for and remove any hardcoded secrets, centralise env-var access, sanitise every user input, reject oversized payloads, and run a full audit. Every story ships as its own commit so the hardening delta is fully traceable.
narrative: The portfolio exposes 6 API endpoints across Sanity content, media delivery, chat, resume, draft-mode, and webhooks. None currently have rate limiting beyond the chat endpoint's built-in limiter. Hardcoded secrets, oversized payloads, and unsanitised inputs are attack vectors that must be closed before the site scales. This slice retrofits every route with a shared rate-limiter, scans the entire monorepo for leaked keys, verifies env-var hygiene, sanitises all user-facing inputs, rejects any payload exceeding safe size limits, and produces a full audit report.
principles: Every endpoint is rate-limited - there is no unprotected route.
Zero hardcoded secrets in tracked files - every key lives in an env var or GitHub secret.
Every user input is validated at the boundary - type-check, length-check, reject malformed.
Oversized payloads are rejected before processing - no endpoint accepts more than it needs.
The audit is the deliverable - findings are documented and fixed, not just reported.

personas.label: Security reviewer
goals: Verify every API route has rate limiting before merge.
Confirm no keys, tokens, or passwords exist in tracked source files.
See a single audit report that enumerates every finding and fix.
painPointsToday: No rate limiting at the application layer on 5 of 6 endpoints.
No systematic scan for leaked secrets has ever been run.
No documented security posture for the marketing site.

personas.label: Future contributor
goals: Know what env vars exist without reading every file.
Add a new endpoint and know the rate-limiting pattern.
Trust that CI will catch a hardcoded secret before merge.
painPointsToday: Env vars are scattered across 8+ modules with no single registry.
No reusable rate-limiter module exists outside of /api/chat.
Input sanitisation is ad-hoc and not documented.

personas.label: PP Namias (owner)
goals: Ship security hardening without breaking existing functionality.
Have a single audit document to share with collaborators.
Know that the site can withstand basic abuse (brute-force, large payloads).
painPointsToday: No visibility into whether endpoints are protected.
Unsure if secrets were ever committed and need rotation.
No documented security baseline for the marketing site.

epics.title: Rate limiting foundation
epics.summary: Build a reusable, parameterised rate-limiter module and apply it to every API route. Auth-adjacent routes (draft-mode enable, live status, webhook) get 5 attempts per 15 minutes. Public routes (chat, resume, media) get higher limits.

stories.title: Create reusable rate-limiter module at src/lib/rate-limiter.ts
stories.details: Extract the Upstash/in-memory dual strategy from src/app/api/chat/lib/rateLimiter.ts into a generic module. Accept parameters: namespace (string, for Redis key scoping), limit (number), windowMs (number). Export a single `createRateLimiter({ namespace, limit, windowMs })` factory returning `isRateLimited(ip: string): Promise<boolean>`. Keep the Upstash fallback chain identical to the chat limiter.
acceptance: Existing chat rate limiter import can be replaced without changing its behaviour.

stories.title: Update /api/chat to use shared rate-limiter
stories.details: Rewrite src/app/api/chat/route.ts to import from src/lib/rate-limiter instead of src/app/api/chat/lib/rateLimiter.ts. Keep the existing limit: 10 requests per 60 seconds. Remove the old chat-specific rateLimiter.ts (its logic lives in the shared module now).
acceptance: Chat endpoint still rate-limited at 10/60s.
Old chat rateLimiter.ts deleted.

stories.title: Add rate limiting to /api/resume
stories.details: Apply the shared rate-limiter with limit=30 per 60 seconds (resume URL lookups are called once per modal open, not chat-frequency). Add getClientIp helper or import from shared utility.
acceptance: Resume endpoint returns 429 when called 31+ times in 60 seconds.

stories.title: Add rate limiting to /api/media/[...path]
stories.details: Apply the shared rate-limiter with limit=100 per 60 seconds (images load in batches on page render). Use IP-based limiting from x-forwarded-for.
acceptance: Media endpoint returns 429 when called 101+ times in 60 seconds.

stories.title: Add strict rate limiting to /api/sanity/webhook (auth route)
stories.details: Apply the shared rate-limiter with limit=5 per 900 seconds (15 minutes). The webhook is called by Sanity CMS on content changes — it should never receive bursts above 5 per 15 minutes. Also check that the existing secret-based authorisation is not bypassed by rate-limiting first.
acceptance: Webhook returns 429 when called 6+ times in 15 minutes.

stories.title: Add strict rate limiting to /api/sanity/live (auth route)
stories.details: Apply the shared rate-limiter with limit=5 per 900 seconds. This endpoint is called by the Sanity Presentation tool's status probe.
acceptance: Live endpoint returns 429 when called 6+ times in 15 minutes.

stories.title: Add strict rate limiting to /api/draft-mode/enable (auth route)
stories.details: Apply the shared rate-limiter with limit=5 per 900 seconds. This endpoint enables preview mode and is called by the Presentation tool iframe.
acceptance: Draft-mode endpoint returns 429 when called 6+ times in 15 minutes.

epics.title: Hardcoded secrets scan
epics.summary: Scan every tracked file in the monorepo for hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, and other secrets. Run both a broad regex scan and a targeted var-name scan. Document every finding. If any real secrets are found, rotate them and purge them from Git history.

stories.title: Run broad regex scan for known key patterns
stories.details: Use grep to search all tracked files (excluding .git, node_modules, .next) for patterns matching common key formats: AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35} (Google), sk-[0-9a-zA-Z]{20,} (OpenAI), ghp_[0-9a-zA-Z]{36} (GitHub PAT), xox[bpras]-[0-9a-zA-Z]{10,} (Slack), AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16} (AWS), and any 32+ char hex/base64 string assigned to a var named key/token/secret/password. Write results to docs/security/scan-report.md.
acceptance: Report lists every match with file:line:column. Report states 'No secrets found' if clean.

stories.title: Run targeted var-name scan for `key`/`token`/`secret`/`password`/`passwd` assignments
stories.details: Search for const/let/var declarations containing 'key', 'token', 'secret', 'password', 'passwd' where the value is a string literal longer than 8 characters. Any hit must be inspected — if it is a real credential, move it to .env (or .env.local) and add the var to .env.example. If it is a test/placeholder value, note it in the report.
acceptance: Report has a section for each match with verdict (real / test / false-positive).

epics.title: Environment variable hygiene
epics.summary: Verify every env var used in the codebase is documented in .env.example, no sensitive var is exposed via NEXT_PUBLIC_, .gitignore covers all secret files, and GitHub Actions workflows do not echo secrets into logs.

stories.title: Reconcile .env.example with all process.env reads in source
stories.details: Grep all `process.env.*` reads across src/ and studio/, extract the variable names, deduplicate, and compare against .env.example. Add any missing vars to .env.example with a placeholder comment. Remove any vars from .env.example that are no longer used.
acceptance: .env.example contains every variable referenced in source, and no unused variables.

stories.title: Verify NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix safety
stories.details: Review every NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable to confirm it is safe for client exposure. By definition, NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars are inlined at build time into the JS bundle. The current set: SANITY_PROJECT_ID, SANITY_DATASET, SANITY_STUDIO_URL, SANITY_CUTOVER_ENABLED, UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID, UMAMI_SCRIPT_URL, UMAMI_HOST_URL, UMAMI_DOMAINS, SITE_URL. Each should be documented as public in .env.example. Flag any that should not be public.
acceptance: Every NEXT_PUBLIC_ var is annotated as 'safe to expose in browser' in .env.example.

stories.title: Verify .gitignore covers all secret-file patterns
stories.details: Check that .env, .env.*, .dev.vars, .wrangler/, and any credential-bearing file patterns are in .gitignore. Confirm no .env file was ever tracked by checking git ls-files for .env*.
acceptance: .gitignore excludes all current env patterns. No .env* file is tracked in Git.

stories.title: Audit GitHub Actions workflows for secret leakage
stories.details: Review every .github/workflows/*.yml for steps that might echo secret values into logs. Confirm all tokens use ${{ secrets.* }} syntax. Check that the react-doctor workflow (just added) does not echo the report JSON into logs (it parses it in node, which is safe).
acceptance: No workflow step echoes a secret value directly. All tokens use GitHub secrets syntax.

epics.title: Input sanitisation & payload limits
epics.summary: Every API endpoint that accepts user input must validate type, length, and structure before processing. Reject oversized payloads at the earliest possible point.

stories.title: Sanitise and bound /api/chat input
stories.details: The chat endpoint already validates message length at 500 chars and checks for string type. Add: strip HTML tags from message and history content (to prevent XSS in future chat-ui rendering), limit history array to 20 entries, limit each history content to 2000 chars, reject message if it contains only whitespace after trim. Add a global 10KB payload limit on the request body.
acceptance: HTML tags in message are stripped. History > 20 entries is truncated. Payload > 10KB returns 413.

stories.title: Sanitise and bound /api/sanity/webhook input
stories.details: The webhook currently reads headers and query params but does not parse a body. Add: validate that the request body (if present) does not exceed 100KB (webhook payloads can include the full document), validate content-type is application/json, and reject any body that is not valid JSON.
acceptance: Non-JSON body returns 400. Body > 100KB returns 413.

stories.title: Add payload size limits to all remaining endpoints
stories.details: Add explicit content-length checks to every route: /api/resume (no body expected — reject any body), /api/media/[...path] (no body expected, reject any body), /api/sanity/live (no body expected, reject any body), /api/draft-mode/enable (handled by next-sanity — verify it already has protection; if not, add 10KB limit). Use a shared helper function.
acceptance: Endpoints that expect no body return 400 when a body is sent.

epics.title: Security audit & report
epics.summary: Run a comprehensive security audit covering all the changes in EPIC-0 through EPIC-3 plus a broader review of cookie flags, CSP headers, dependency vulnerabilities, and TLS configuration. Produce a single audit document.

stories.title: Run automated npm audit and review dependencies
stories.details: Run npm audit on both root package.json and studio/package.json. Document any critical/high vulnerabilities. If fixable with npm audit fix, do it. If not, document the advisory and mitigation.
acceptance: Audit report lists every vulnerability, its severity, and whether it was fixed or documented as a risk.

stories.title: Review HTTP security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
stories.details: Check next.config.js and the Cloudflare Workers response for security headers. The site currently serves behind Workers; verify that headers like X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security are set either in Workers config, next.config.js, or a middleware. If missing, add them.
acceptance: Audit report has a section on each header with 'Set' or 'Missing' status. Missing headers are added to next.config.ts or middleware.

stories.title: Review secure cookie flags (draft-mode, sessionStorage usage)
stories.details: Check that draft-mode cookies set HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax. Review client-side sessionStorage usage (hub_interacted, booking event key) — these are not sensitive but should be documented. Confirm no auth tokens are stored in sessionStorage or localStorage.
acceptance: Audit report documents cookie flags and storage usage. Any missing flags are flagged for fix.

stories.title: Write final security audit report
stories.details: Compile all findings from S-4.1 through S-4.3 and the completed fixes from EPIC-0..3 into docs/security/audit.md. Include: endpoints covered, rate-limit tiers, secrets scan result, env-var hygiene status, input sanitisation coverage, payload limits, header status, cookie flags, and dependency vulnerabilities. End with an overall security posture summary.
acceptance: Audit report is a standalone document that fully describes the security posture of the marketing site.
